text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigeria's military government has approved a revised timetable for elections, with multi-party polls for both the presidency and regional governorships to be held on August 1, 1998.

- Interior Minister Baba Gana Kingibe told the British High Commissioner (ambassador) it was disappointing to all Nigerians that the former colonial power did not play a bigger role in defending Nigeria on the international stage.
- Permits for prospective operators of radio and television stations have increased in price to between one and five million naira, from less than 500,000 naira before.
- A 20-member delegation from United States National Baptist Convention Holdings met senior officials at the stock exchange to explore the possibility of investing in Nigeria.
- Britain may not review its tough stand on Nigeria until the transition programme to civilian rule is implemented next year.
- Oil minister Dan Etete complained about low Nigerian participation in the oil sector.
- Savannah Bank has resumed advertising after a four year break, which some have blamed on the bank's internal crisis.
- Ethnic Ijaw communities in southern Delta state have given Shell an ultimatum to quit their oil-producing areas or be forced out.
- Nigeria Airways faces a fresh debt crisis of around $31 million after a recent London court went against the national carrier.
- Nigerian Breweries and Guinness Nigeria have called for an urgent review of taxes and duties, to ensure the survival of the brewing industry.
